themes.label: SVI construction and identification methodology
themes.need: Someone building or replicating a Google-search-based investor attention measure across a large stock universe needs the ticker-vs-company-name identification rule, the noisy-generic-ticker exclusion, the MSFT cross-sectional normalization procedure, and the underlying data/sample construction.
themes.distributed_justification: The intro's rationale for a direct, ticker-based search attention measure (b004-b005) is resolved by the full construction methodology in Section 2 (b014-b019, b023) and the normalization procedure illustrated in the Figure 1 caption (b068) -- one distributed 'how is SVI built' need.

themes.label: SVI level/change distinctness from attention proxies
themes.need: Someone wants to know whether the level and week-to-week change in Google search attention (SVI) is statistically distinct from -- not redundant with -- existing indirect attention proxies (market cap, turnover, news occurrence, analyst coverage, advertising expense), via correlation and regression evidence.
themes.distributed_justification: Intro critique of indirect proxies and preview of the distinctness finding (b002-b003, b006, b031) is resolved by Section 3's correlation/regression evidence (b020, b024-b028) and its supporting Tables 1-3 at the document's end (b071-b073) -- one distributed 'is SVI redundant with existing proxies' need.

themes.label: SVI lead-lag relative to attention proxies (VAR)
themes.need: Someone wants to know whether search-attention spikes temporally precede or follow extreme returns, turnover, and news occurrence, to test whether investors search for a stock in anticipation of information events.
themes.distributed_justification: The VAR setup and results (b029-b030) are backed by the full Table 4 VAR data placed at the document's end (b074) -- one distributed 'does SVI lead or lag other attention measures' need.

themes.label: SVI and individual/retail investor trading via Dash-5
themes.need: Someone wanting to confirm which type of investor (retail vs institutional, sophisticated vs unsophisticated) Google search attention actually captures needs the Dash-5 order-data methodology and the regression evidence linking SVI changes to individual trading, split across market centers of differing investor sophistication.
themes.distributed_justification: Intro preview that SVI plausibly captures retail attention (b007) and the Dash-5 data source note (b022) are resolved in Section 4's full methodology and market-center comparison (b032-b044), backed by Table 5's regression data at the document's end (b075-b076) -- one distributed 'whose attention does SVI capture' need.

themes.label: SVI changes and Russell 3000 price pressure
themes.need: Someone testing whether search-attention increases predict short-term price pressure across the broader stock universe (beyond IPOs) needs the Russell 3000 portfolio-sort and panel-regression evidence on SVI_Change and subsequent returns, especially among small-cap stocks.
themes.distributed_justification: The small-cap price-pressure preview in the intro (b010) is resolved by Section 5.2's portfolio and regression analysis (b056-b060), backed by Tables 8-9 at the document's end (b079-b081) -- one distributed 'does SVI predict Russell-wide price pressure' need.

themes.label: Level of SVI and price momentum: DHS vs Hong-Stein
themes.need: Someone trying to distinguish between overreaction (Daniel-Hirshleifer-Subrahmanyam) and slow-information-diffusion (Hong-Stein) explanations of price momentum needs the evidence on how weekly price-momentum profits differ between high- and low-SVI stocks, robust to size, analyst coverage and alternative attention proxies.
themes.distributed_justification: The momentum-motivation and the two rival theories previewed in the intro (b011-b013) are resolved by Section 6's full momentum analysis (b061-b067), backed by Tables 10-11 at the document's end (b082-b086) -- one distributed 'which momentum theory does SVI-level evidence support' need.
